means: The radial or parallel field of lines that fills the whole background of a manga panel. Same ink language as motion lines, but applied to the FRAME rather than to an object.
does: Replaces the background with a burst of converging lines. That is simultaneously the point and the danger - it will delete the location you established two shots ago, which is exactly right at the peak of an impact and destructive on a shot that still needs to read as a stadium. Direction is worth naming: 'radial speed lines' converge on the subject and hit hardest, horizontal ones read as lateral speed. It is near-synonymous with motion lines and with 'emphasis lines', and stacking all three does not compound - it just spends tag slots.
reach_for_it: the peak of an action beat, once the background has already done its job and can be sacrificed
used_in: 14 uses across derby.json, episode01.json and her-name.json - the most-used effect tag in the set. her-name.json writes 'radial speed lines filling the frame' on its two biggest hits. Exposed in the authoring layer as shot.fx.speed_lines with radial, horizontal, vertical, impact and motion_trail variants
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
